'''José Juan Barea Mora''' (born June 26, 1984) is a Puerto Rican [[basketball]] coach and former player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern Huskies]] before joining the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2006 and becoming the seventh Puerto Rican to play in the NBA. He went on to win an NBA championship with the Mavericks in 2011 before signing with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], where he played for the next three seasons before returning to Dallas. He has also played in the [[NBA Development League]] and the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].

Barea was a member of the [[Puerto Rican national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]] that won the gold medal in the 2006 and 2010 [[Central American and Caribbean Games]]. He was the starting point guard for Puerto Rico when they won the gold medal in the [[2011 Pan American Games]] and the silver medal in the [[2007 Pan American Games]].

Barea served as head coach of [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) in 2024 and 2025.

==Early life==
Barea was born in the municipality of [[Mayagüez, Puerto Rico|Mayagüez]] in the west coast of Puerto Rico in 1984 to parents Marta (née Mora) and Jaime Barea.<ref>{{cite web| last=Sánchez-Bretón | first=Raúl Álzaga | url=http://www.primerahora.com/noticia/baloncesto/accion_deportiva/barea__pronostica_un_anillo_de_campeonato/27302| title=Barea pronostica un anillo de campeonato| work=PrimeraHora.com | language=es| date=February 17, 2007| access-date=July 27, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070929092821/http://www.primerahora.com/noticia/baloncesto/accion_deportiva/barea__pronostica_un_anillo_de_campeonato/27302 |archive-date = September 29, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=wfaa>{{cite web| url=http://www.wfaa.com/story/sports/nba/mavericks/2014/08/13/13738660/| title=J.J. Barea's family in Dallas for The Finals| work=WFAA.com| date=June 7, 2011| access-date=October 28, 2014| archive-date=October 28, 2014| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028122316/http://www.wfaa.com/story/sports/nba/mavericks/2014/08/13/13738660/| url-status=dead}}</ref> With a father who was an engineer and a mother who was a retired professor as well as volleyball and tennis coach, he grew up in an upper-middle-class neighborhood of Mayagüez.<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24785945/inside-unique-bond-puerto-rico-native-son-jj-barea-nba|title=The people know that Jose Juan is part of Puerto Rico. He feels it.|date=September 26, 2018|publisher=ESPN|language=en}}</ref> Barea was a member of [[Scouting in Puerto Rico|Boy Scouts of America]] Troop 790 for seven years. He graduated from [[Academia de la Inmaculada Concepción]] high school.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/31273922/Tu-Revista-Es-Vida-2010| title=Tu Revista Es Vida 2010| via=Scribd | date=May 22, 2010| access-date=October 28, 2014|language=es}}</ref>

In 2001, Barea started playing basketball for [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). Later that year, he moved to Florida to attend high school at [[Miami Christian School]] in [[Miami, Florida]]. As a senior in 2001–02, he averaged 20 points, 6 rebounds, 8 assists, and 3 steals in helping his team to the state title and a 38–2 record. He made a name for himself nationally at the City of Palms event in December 2001 where he was the team's leading scorer and showcased an accurate shot from three-point range.<ref name=scout>{{cite web | last=Telep | first=Dave | url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/2/45744.htm| title=Barea headed north| work=Scout.com | date=April 24, 2002| access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> In April 2002, he enrolled at [[Northeastern University]].<ref name="scout" />

After attending Northeastern University, Barea returned to Puerto Rico to rejoin Indios de Mayagüez for the 2002 BSN season; there, he averaged 2.8 points in 14 games.<ref name=bsnpr>{{cite web| url=http://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador.asp?id=1234&| archive-url=https://archive.today/20141028101302/http://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador.asp?id=1234&| url-status=dead| archive-date=October 28, 2014| title=Estadísticas Jugador – Barea Mora, José Juan| work=bsnpr.com| access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman playing for the [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern Huskies]] in 2002–03, Barea earned third-team All-[[America East Conference]] (AEC) and AEC All-Rookie team honors, after averaging a conference-leading 17 points to go along with 3 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 1.9 steals in 28 contests. He became the first freshman in Husky basketball history to record 400 points and 100 assists in a season and accrued a team-high 25 games of scoring in double-figures.<ref name=bio>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/Jose%20JuanBarea.html| title=Prospect Profile: Jose Juan Barea| publisher=National Basketball Association| access-date=October 28, 2014| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119223347/http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/Jose%20JuanBarea.html| archive-date=January 19, 2015| df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jose-barea-1.html |title=Jose Barea Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=October 28, 2014 |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028125536/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jose-barea-1.html |archive-date=October 28, 2014 }}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2003–04, Barea earned First Team All-America East honors after finishing second in that conference for both scoring (20.7 ppg) and assists (5.8 apg) and becoming the first Husky since [[Reggie Lewis]] in 1986–87 to average at least 20 points per game.<ref name="Northeastern bio" /><ref name="stats" />

As a junior in 2004–05, Barea ranked second in the America East and eighth in the country in scoring (22.2 ppg); he also led the conference and was fifth in the nation in assists (7.3 apg). He later earned first-team All-AEC honors for the second consecutive year. Further, he placed third in assists (218), fourth in three-pointers (68), and sixth in points (665) on Northeastern's single-season charts, and tied the school record with a career-high 41 points against the [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook Seawolves]]. He was also named a finalist for the illustrious [[Bob Cousy]] Award.<ref name="Northeastern bio" /><ref name="stats" />

As a senior in 2005–06, Barea was named Honorable Mention All-America by [[The Associated Press]], the Player of the Year in the [[Coastal Athletic Association|Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA), first-team All-CAA, first-team NABC All-District One, and [[Lou Henson Award|Mid-Major Player of the Year]] by [[CollegeInsider.com]]. He led Northeastern and finished third in the nation in assists (8.4 apg), and he finished 19th in the nation in scoring (21.0 ppg). Barea was yet again named a finalist for the Bob Cousy Award.<ref name="Northeastern bio">{{cite web|url=http://gonu.com:80/mbasketball/barea.shtml|title=#5 Jose Juan Barea|work=GoNU.com|publisher=Northeastern University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060418123915/http://gonu.com/mbasketball/barea.shtml|archive-date=April 18, 2006|access-date=April 4, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Barea finished his collegiate career as the school's second all-time leading scorer, with 2,209 points behind Reggie Lewis, and he left Northeastern as its second all-time leader in assists, with 721, and its leader in three-point field goals made (255).<ref name="bio" />

===Post-college===
In April 2006, Barea had a productive performance at the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]] in [[Virginia]], finishing with averages of 14.0 points, 13.7 assists, and 5.7 rebounds per game in three contests.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/features/portsmouth_060410.html| title=Saving the Best for Last at PIT| publisher=National Basketball Association| date=April 9, 2006| access-date=May 19, 2007| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121111023313/http://www.nba.com/features/portsmouth_060410.html| archive-date=November 11, 2012| url-status=dead}}</ref> Barea broke the single-game and single-tournament assist records, as he dished out 18 assists for Beach Barton Ford in a 118–100 victory over Norfolk Sports Club, giving him 41 assists in three games. For his efforts, Barea received the tournament's first [[Allen Iverson]] A.I. award, given to the player deemed most important to his team.<ref>{{cite web| last=Hoy| first=Shaun| url=https://www.dailypress.com/2006/04/09/portsmouth-sports-club-claims-pit-championship/| title=Portsmouth Sports Club Claims Pit Championship| work=DailyPress.com| date=April 9, 2006| access-date=October 28, 2014| archive-date=October 28, 2014| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028113156/http://articles.dailypress.com/2006-04-09/sports/0604090045_1_northeastern-s-jose-juan-barea-holiday-inn-pit| url-status=live}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2006)===
After the Portsmouth Invitational Tournament, Barea returned to Puerto Rico to join [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] for the 2006 BSN season, where he averaged 10.4 points, 2.7 assists, and 2.8 rebounds over 9 games.<ref name="bsnpr" />

===Dallas Mavericks (2006–2011)===

====2006–09: early years====
After going undrafted in the [[2006 NBA draft]], Barea joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the 2006 [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] where in five games, he averaged 6.8 points, 1.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists, and 2 steals in 21.4 minutes per contest.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Golden-State-Warriors/9/Rosters/Summer_League/2006| title=2006–2007 Golden State Warriors Summer League Rosters| work=RealGM.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> He then joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[Rocky Mountain Revue]] where in three games, he averaged 12.0 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 6.7 assists in 25.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Dallas-Mavericks/6/Rosters/Summer_League/2006| title=2006–2007 Dallas Mavericks Summer League Rosters| work=RealGM.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On August 17, 2006, Barea signed a multi-year deal with the Dallas Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2552880| title=Mavericks sign four free agents, including Ebi| publisher=ESPN | date=August 17, 2006 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> On November 4, 2006, he made his regular season debut for the franchise, recording two points in two and a half minutes of action during a 76–107 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261104010| archive-url=https://archive.today/20141028101333/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261104010| url-status=dead| archive-date=October 28, 2014| title=This time around, Yao, Rockets plow through Mavs| publisher=ESPN | date=November 4, 2006 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On January 17, 2007, Barea was assigned to the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/barea-dleague-011707.shtml| title=Mavericks assign Jose Juan Barea to D-League | work=InsideHoops.com | date=January 17, 2007 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> On January 29, he was named the D-League Performer of the Week after he topped 40 points in two different games while leading the Flyers to a 3–1 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/performer_070129.html | title=D-League Performer of the Week: January 29, 2007 | publisher=National Basketball Association | date=January 29, 2007 | access-date=October 28, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070331154503/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/performer_070129.html | archive-date=March 31, 2007 | df=mdy-all }}</ref> On February 1, 2007, he was recalled by the Mavericks after he averaged 27.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.8 assists, and 1.3 steals in eight D-League games.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/b/bareajo01d.html| title=Jose Barea D-League Stats | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On April 13, 2007, Barea recorded a season-high 16 points in an 89–104 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]]. Four days later, he started his first career game for the Mavericks in which he contributed 13 points, 10 rebounds, and 3 assists during an 82–111 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Barea finished his rookie season with averages of 2.4 points, 0.5 rebounds, 0.8 assists, and 0.7 steals in 33 regular season games. He also played two playoff games for the Mavericks, scoring 0 points in three and a half total minutes.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bareajo01/gamelog/2007/| title=Jose Barea 2006–07 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2007, Barea re-joined the Dallas Mavericks for the 2007 Las Vegas Summer League, where in five games, he averaged 16.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 7.0 assists in 27.6 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Dallas-Mavericks/6/Rosters/Summer_League/2007| title=2007–2008 Dallas Mavericks Summer League Rosters| work=RealGM.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On November 3, 2007, he recorded a then career-high 25 points in a 123–102 victory over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271103006| archive-url=https://archive.today/20120708182118/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271103006| url-status=dead| archive-date=July 8, 2012| title=Barea's career-high 25 in second start key Mavs' rout of Kings| publisher=ESPN | date=November 3, 2007 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> He went on to appear in 44 regular season games (with 9 starts) for the Mavericks in 2007–08 while averaging 4.3 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 1.3 assists in 10.5 minutes per game. He also managed one playoff game where he contributed eight points against the [[New Orleans Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bareajo01/gamelog/2008/| title=Jose Barea 2007–08 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On July 9, 2008, Barea re-signed with the Dallas Mavericks to a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/mavs-sign-barea-070908.shtml| title=Mavericks re-sign Jose Juan Barea | work=InsideHoops.com | date=July 9, 2008 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> In [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]], Barea's role on the team increased dramatically. Injuries to [[Jerry Stackhouse]], [[Josh Howard]], and [[Jason Terry]] saw Barea's minutes per game double as coach [[Rick Carlisle]] began regularly using a three-guard lineup which included [[Jason Kidd]], [[Jason Terry]], and Barea to spark an offensive streak in games. On February 20, 2009, Barea scored a then career high 26 points during an 86–93 loss to the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290220010| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090224233447/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290220010| url-status=dead| archive-date=February 24, 2009| title=Brooks hits 3-pointer with 24 seconds left as Rockets survive Mavs| publisher=ESPN | date=February 20, 2009 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In the [[2009 NBA Playoffs|2009 playoffs]], Barea became a starter during the first round, replacing [[Antoine Wright (basketball)|Antoine Wright]] in an effort to contain [[Tony Parker]] of the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He put up 13 points and added 7 assists in his first playoff start.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290423006| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090425173123/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290423006| url-status=dead| archive-date=April 25, 2009| title=Mavs grab upper hand with Game 3 demolition of Spurs| publisher=ESPN | date=April 23, 2009 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

====2009–11: first championship====
In [[2009–10 NBA season|the 2009–10]] season, Barea again played an important role off the bench for the Mavericks. Over 78 games (with 18 starts), he averaged 7.6 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 3.3 assists in 19.8 minutes per game. He scored a season-high 23 points twice during the season and played in all six of the Mavericks' playoff games, where they once again fell to the San Antonio Spurs in the first round.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bareajo01/gamelog/2010/| title=Jose Barea 2009–10 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In June 2010, the Mavericks exercised their $1.8 million 2010–11 team option on Barea's contract.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/203815/Dallas_Will_Pick_Up_Bareas_Option| title=Dallas Will Pick Up Barea's Option | work=RealGM.com | date=May 11, 2010 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>[[File:JJ Barea.jpg|thumb|Barea playing for Dallas]]
In [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11]], Barea played a career-high 81 regular season games, averaging 9.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 3.9 assists in 20.6 minutes per contest. On January 1, 2011, he scored a then career-high 29 points in an 87–99 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310101015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110105092533/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310101015| url-status=dead| archive-date=January 5, 2011| title=Earl Boykins' season-best 26 points lift Bucks past banged-up Mavs| publisher=ESPN | date=January 1, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In the second round of the [[2011 NBA Playoffs|2011 playoffs]], the Mavericks faced off against the defending champions, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. During the second game of the series, Barea converted 12 points coming off the bench to lead a fourth-quarter rally that secured the 93–81 win for Dallas. With the game already decided and 24 seconds remaining, Barea was clotheslined by Lakers' Center Andrew Bynum for which Bynum was subsequently suspended.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310504013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110508033404/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310504013| url-status=dead| archive-date=May 8, 2011| title=Dirk Nowitzki, Mavs win in L.A. again to go up 2–0 on Lakers| publisher=ESPN | date=May 4, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> After the game, the Lakers praised Barea's performance with [[Phil Jackson]] even comparing him to star point guard [[Chris Paul]], while [[Kobe Bryant]] went on record saying that "Barea kicked our asses".<ref>{{cite web|last=Sefko |first=Eddie |url=http://mavsblog.dallasnews.com/2011/05/kobe-bryant-staying-calm-amid-all-the-dr.html/ |title=Kobe Bryant: Barea's success wasn't Dirk's doing; J.J. 'kicked our ass' |work=The Dallas Morning News |date=May 6, 2011 |access-date=October 28, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028112736/http://mavsblog.dallasnews.com/2011/05/kobe-bryant-staying-calm-amid-all-the-dr.html/ |archive-date=October 28, 2014 }}</ref>

The Mavericks won the final game of the series to advance past the Lakers. Barea was the second-leading scorer for his team, putting up 22 points to go along with 8 assists. At one point in the fourth quarter, Barea had darted down the lane and was in midair about to finish a layup when Lakers' center [[Andrew Bynum]] threw him an elbow; the flagrant foul caused Barea to fall down hard and Bynum to be immediately ejected.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/news/story?id=6522694| title=Andrew Bynum suspended, fined| publisher=ESPN | date=May 11, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> Barea recovered, however, and played the rest of the game. He called the foul "dangerous". Initially Bynum was unapologetic about the incident, saying, "We were getting embarrassed. They were breaking us down. So I just fouled somebody." He later issued a formal apology to the league and to Barea.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/news/story?id=6521032| title=Andrew Bynum sorry for decking Barea| publisher=ESPN | date=May 10, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> The NBA suspended Bynum for the first five games in the next season in consequence, but later shortened the suspension to four games due to the lockout-shortened season.

The Mavericks advanced to the [[2011 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where they faced the [[Miami Heat]] led by the trio of Dwyane Wade, Chris Bosh, and Lebron James. Coach Rick Carlisle decided to start Barea when they were down 1–2 in the series. Barea became a key player, being instrumental in changing the dynamic of the entire series and winning the next three games. The Mavericks defeated the Heat 4 games to 2 and so claimed their first NBA championship in franchise history. Barea became the second Puerto Rican player to ever win an NBA championship, following [[Butch Lee]] in 1980.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/senadogalardonagestadejosejuanbarea-515134/| title=Senado galardona gesta de José Juan Barea| work=PrimeraHora.com | date=June 13, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014|language=es}}</ref> Barea started in three of 21 playoff games that he played for the Mavericks, while averaging 8.9 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 3.4 assists in 18.6 minutes per game.

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2011–2014)===
[[File:José Juan Barea-MN v DET.jpg|thumb|left|Barea before a game in 2012]]

After failed negotiations to re-sign with the Mavericks, Barea began looking elsewhere, but, because of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]], he was unable to sign with another franchise. On December 14, 2011, following the conclusion of the lockout, Barea signed a four-year, $19 million contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8834| title=Timberwolves sign Jose Juan Barea| work=InsideHoops.com | date=December 14, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/12/14/wolves-barea.ap/index.html| title=Timberwolves welcome guard Barea to Minnesota| publisher=National Basketball Association | date=December 14, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

On December 26, 2011, Barea made his debut for the Timberwolves, recording 14 points, 2 assists, and 2 rebounds in a 100–104 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=311226016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111227061814/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=311226016| url-status=dead| archive-date=December 27, 2011| title=Kevin Durant scores 33 as Thunder keep Wolves at bay| publisher=ESPN | date=December 26, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> However, Barea's season was hampered with ankle and thigh injuries as he managed only 41 of 66 games for the Timberwolves in 2011–12. Despite this, on March 23, 2012, Barea recorded his first career [[Double (basketball)#Triple-double|triple-double]], putting up 25 points along with 10 rebounds and 14 assists in a 149–140 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/minnesota-timberwolves-oklahoma-city-thunder-2012032325/| title=Minnesota at Oklahoma City| publisher=Yahoo!| date=March 23, 2012| access-date=October 28, 2014| archive-date=October 28, 2014| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028133822/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/minnesota-timberwolves-oklahoma-city-thunder-2012032325/| url-status=dead}}</ref> During the last weeks of the season, and with injuries to starters [[Ricky Rubio]], [[Kevin Love]], and [[Luke Ridnour]], Barea became the starting point guard, averaging 15.8 points and 9.4 assists during the last 9 games. During that period, Barea tallied a season-high 28 points and a career-high 15 assists.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bareajo01/gamelog/2012/| title=Jose Barea 2011–12 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

Barea began the season with 21 points and 5 assists against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on November 2, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121102/SACMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Wolves 92, Kings 80|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 2, 2012|access-date=November 2, 2012}}</ref> However, in his fourth game, he sprained his left foot, which caused him to miss the next five contests.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/balanced-wolves-drill-magic-90-032434859--nba.html|title=Balanced Wolves drill Magic, 90–75|publisher=Yahoo!|last=Krawczynski|first=Jon|date=November 7, 2012|access-date=November 7, 2012|archive-date=March 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170325114710/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/balanced-wolves-drill-magic-90-032434859--nba.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In December, Barea averaged more than 25 minutes and 12.7 points per game coming off the bench. He had his best game of the season on April 12, when he scored 23 points against the [[Utah Jazz]]. He finished that season with averages of 11.3 points, 4.0 assists, and 2.8 rebounds in 23.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bareajo01/gamelog/2013/| title=Jose Barea 2012–13 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14]], Barea served as the Timberwolves back-up point guard behind [[Ricky Rubio]]. He had his best offensive game on November 15, against the [[Denver Nuggets]], scoring 21 points to go with 4 assists. In January, Timberwolves star [[Kevin Love]] indirectly criticized teammates Barea and [[Dante Cunningham]] for their behavior during game timeouts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/01/09/wolves-love-bench.ap/|title=Love criticizes teammates after Wolves' loss|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 9, 2014|access-date=July 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150428045549/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/01/09/wolves-love-bench.ap|archive-date=April 28, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barea finished the season averaging 8.4 points and 3.8 assists per game.

On October 27, 2014, Barea was waived by the Timberwolves<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-set-2014-15-opening-night-roster|title=Timberwolves Set 2014–15 Opening Night Roster|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> in the hope of returning to the Dallas Mavericks.<ref>{{cite news|last=Moore|first=Matt|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24770852/reports-wolves-to-buy-out-jj-barea-who-wants-to-sign-with-mavericks|title=Report: J.J. Barea to sign with Dallas after being waived by Wolves|work=CBSSports.com|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

==National team career==
Barea began his international career with Puerto Rico's Under-19 junior national team, participating in the [[2003 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] where he tied for third place in the tournament's [[Most Valuable Player]] poll.<ref>{{cite web|title= World Championship for Juniors 2007| url=http://www.eurobasket.com/events/wcu18/wcjun07.asp |publisher=Eurobasket.com| date=July 20, 2003| access-date=May 20, 2007 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070207075457/http://www.eurobasket.com/events/wcu18/wcjun07.asp |archive-date = February 7, 2007}}</ref> His next international performance occurred at [[Caguas, Puerto Rico]], in the Under-21 Centrobasket tournament, in which Puerto Rico won the gold medal. Barea was awarded the Most Valuable Player award after leading the tournament in scoring, assists, and steals. His last participation at the Under-21 level was at the 2005 [[FIBA Under-21 World Championship]], where he finished fourth in scoring with an average of 17.6 points per game and led the competition in assists with 7.3 per game, as Puerto Rico took seventh.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gonu.com/mbasketball/news/barea081705.htm |title=Barea stars in Under-21 World Championships |publisher=North Eastern University |date=August 17, 2005 |access-date=May 20, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070223154745/http://www.gonu.com/mbasketball/news/barea081705.htm |archive-date=February 23, 2007 }}</ref>

In July 2006, Barea made his debut for the senior [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|national team]] in the 2006 [[Central American and Caribbean Games]], where Puerto Rico captured the gold medal. In the championship game against Panama, Barea drilled the decisive three-point basket with fourteen seconds left to give Puerto Rico a final advantage. Puerto Rico finished the tournament undefeated after six straight victories. Barea was then named the tournament's Most Valuable Player. He was the primary point guard for the Puerto Rican team that won the silver medal in the [[Basketball at the 2007 Pan American Games|2007 Pan American Games]].<ref>{{cite web| author=Alex Figueroa| url=http://nuevo.primerahora.com/XStatic/primerahora/template/nota.aspx?n=94712| title=Brasil ganó y Puerto Rico se llevó plata|work=Primera Hora| language=es| date=July 29, 2007| access-date=August 2, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070929093458/http://nuevo.primerahora.com/XStatic/primerahora/template/nota.aspx?n=94712 |archive-date = September 29, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> Later that year, he played limited minutes in the [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]], where Puerto Rico won the bronze medal. In 2008, Barea partook in a series of preparatory tournaments before the [[2008 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|2008 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]].<ref>{{cite book| author=Raúl Álzaga Sánchez-Bretón| title=Boricuas debutan con triunfo ante Alemania|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=July 4, 2008| chapter=Deportes}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| title=Derrota ante los griegos|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=July 5, 2008| chapter=Deportes}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| title=Puerto Rico vence a Nueva Zelanda en baloncesto|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=July 8, 2008| chapter=Deportes}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| title=Puerto Rico vence a Irán 83–80|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=July 9, 2008| chapter=Deportes}}</ref> In these [[exhibition games]], he played in the starting lineup. The Olympic Qualifying Tournament began on July 14, 2008, with Barea returning to the back-up [[point guard]] position behind [[Carlos Arroyo]]. Puerto Rico advanced to the finals, but did not qualify to the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite book| title=Con la cabeza en alto Puerto Rico| author=José R. Ortúzar|work=[[El Vocero]]| language=es| date=July 21, 2008}}</ref> In this tournament, Barea had averages of 12.4 points, 2.2 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.athens2008.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olymQual/men/teamPlay/play/p/competitioncode//eventid/4508/langid/1/langlc/en/playernumber/44405/roundid/4508/season//teamnumber/349/fe_teamPlay_playStat.html| title=Player Statistics – Juan Jose Barea| publisher=FIBA (2008 Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men)| access-date=July 25, 2008| archive-url=https://archive.today/20120727231845/http://www.athens2008.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olymQual/men/teamPlay/play/p/competitioncode//eventid/4508/langid/1/langlc/en/playernumber/44405/roundid/4508/season//teamnumber/349/fe_teamPlay_playStat.html| archive-date=July 27, 2012| url-status=dead}}</ref>

Barea continued playing backup point guard at the [[2008 Centrobasket]] tournament and entered the final round leading the event in points, after scoring 31 and 30 against Panama and the Dominican Republic, respectively.<ref>{{cite book| title=Luce Barea para mantener invicto de Puerto Rico|  work=[[El Vocero]]| language=es| date=August 30, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| title=Puerto Rico va por el oro|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=August 21, 2008|chapter=Deportes}}</ref> In the last two games, Barea was promoted to the starting lineup. Puerto Rico went on to claim the gold medal of the tournament, by defeating the United States Virgin Islands, and Barea to receive its Most Valuable Player award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaamericas.com/noticiasread_us.asp?r=PUZNIPUXDT |title=PUR – Jose Juan Barea MVP of Centrobasket Tournament |publisher=FIBA Americas |date=September 1, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080915050153/http://www.fibaamericas.com/noticiasread_us.asp?r=PUZNIPUXDT |archive-date=September 15, 2008 }}</ref> In 2009, the Mavericks declined to allow Barea to participate in the [[FIBA Americas Championship 2009|FIBA Americas Championship]] for fear that he might re-injure his left shoulder after having recently undergone post-season surgery to repair it.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/josejuanbareanopodrajugarenelpremundial-323121/| title=José Juan Barea no podrá jugar en el Premundial| author=Lester Jiménez|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=August 12, 2009| access-date=October 17, 2009}}</ref> Barea returned to international play at the [[2010 Centrobasket]], serving as the national team's starting point guard, while Arroyo was moved to the regular [[shooting guard]] position.<ref>{{cite book| title=José Juan Barea y Carlos Arroyo: el dúo dinámico boricua| author=José Ayala Gordián|work=[[Primera Hora (Guaynabo)|Primera Hora]]| language=es| date=July 13, 2010| chapter=Deportes}}</ref> Puerto Rico ousted Panama in the semi-finals and the Dominican Republic in the finals to capture the gold medal. Barea averaged 13.8 points and led CentroBasket in assists per game, with 7; for his efforts, he clinched a spot on the All-Star Team for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://diadeportivo.com/noticia.php?noticiaId=8612&nombre=Puerto-Rico-campe%F3n-de-CentroBasket-2010 |title=Puerto Rico campeón de CentroBasket 2010 |author=Wilson Tavárez |publisher=DiaDeportivo.com |language=es |date=July 12, 2010 |access-date=July 13, 2010 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814145929/http://diadeportivo.com/noticia.php?noticiaId=8612 |archive-date=August 14, 2011 }}</ref>

Barea helped Puerto Rico take home a silver medal at the [[2013 FIBA Americas Championship]], and he was named to the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. He was also on the roster of the [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|national team]] that played in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. Although Puerto Rico was eliminated in the second round, Barea finished as [[FIBA World Cup Top Scorer|the World Cup Top Scorer]] during the First Round. He accumulated 110 points in 5 contests for an average of 22 [[points per game]]. Barea's scoring statistics proved above even such talents as [[Luis Scola]], [[Andray Blatche]], [[Pau Gasol]], and [[Francisco García (basketball)|Francisco García]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/barealomejordepuertoricoenelmundial-1847872.html|title=Barea: lo mejor de Puerto Rico en el Mundial|author=Rosa Rosa, Carlos|work=[[El Nuevo Día]]|date=September 4, 2014|access-date=September 5, 2014|archive-date=September 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140907130059/http://www.elnuevodia.com/barealomejordepuertoricoenelmundial-1847872.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 30 May 2017, Barea was appointed the head coach of [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] for the rest of the 2017 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Barea to coach team in Puerto Rican League |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19498123/puerto-rican-team-hires-jj-barea-dallas-mavericks-coach-rest-season |access-date=10 May 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=30 May 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

On 15 August 2021, Barea was hired by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as a player development coach.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title="J.J. Barea: 'I like coaching. Every time I do it, I like it even more'"|url=https://www.mavs.com/barea-coach/|website=Mavs.com|date=15 August 2021|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref> He concluded his duties by the end of the year.<ref name=sights>{{cite news |title=J.J. In August 2023, Barea was appointed the head coach of [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] for the [[2024 Baloncesto Superior Nacional season|2024 BSN season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Report: Former NBA Guard J.J. ==Personal life==
While listed as {{convert|6|ft|0|in|abbr=on}} by the NBA, Barea's mother believes his actual height is around {{convert|5|ft|10|in|abbr=on}}.<ref name="wfaa" /> In a 2016 ''[[The Wall Street Journal|Wall Street Journal]]'' story, Barea said that when announced as being 6 feet in pregame player introductions, he sometimes had to stop himself from giggling "because me and about 20,000 other people in the arena knew that was a lie."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/23913544/the-body-issue-getting-athlete-real-measurements-rarely-easy |title=Tall tales: Getting an athlete's real measurements is rarely easy |first=David |last=Fleming |publisher=ESPN |date=June 27, 2018 |access-date=June 27, 2018}}</ref> In September 2019, Barea was officially measured by the Mavericks organization and was found to stand {{convert|5|ft|10|in|abbr=on}} barefoot.<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2019/09/30/mavericks-tales-of-the-tape-j-j-barea-no-longer-a-6-footer-porzingis-comes-in-just-shorter-than-boban/|title=Mavericks tales of the tape: J.J. In March 2011, Barea confirmed he was in a relationship with [[Miss Universe 2006]] [[Zuleyka Rivera]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Caplan | first=Jeff | url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6272724| title=J.J. Barea dating Miss Universe 2006| publisher=ESPN | date=March 30, 2011 | access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> In July 2011, they confirmed that they were expecting their first child.<ref>{{cite web|last=Castillo|first=Amaris|url=http://www.latina.com/entertainment/buzz/former-miss-universe-zuleyka-rivera-pregnant-nba-star-jj-bareas-baby|title=Former Miss Universe Zuleyka Rivera pregnant with NBA star JJ Barea's baby!|date=July 21, 2011|work=Latina.com|access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> Rivera gave birth to their son Sebastián José Barea Rivera on February 17, 2012. Barea was present during the birth.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/zuleykariveradaaluzasebastianjose-1193548.html|title=Zuleyka Rivera da a luz a Sebastián José|last=Hernández Mercado|first=Damaris|date=February 17, 2012|work=elnuevodia.com|access-date=February 17, 2012|language=es|trans-title=Zuleyka Rivera gives birth to Sebastián José|archive-date=December 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222191922/http://www.elnuevodia.com/zuleykariveradaaluzasebastianjose-1193548.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The couple later split in April 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/zuleykaybareaterminaronsurelacion-1493649.html|title=Zuleyka y Barea terminaron su relación|work=elnuevodia.com|date=April 18, 2013|access-date=April 18, 2013|language=es|archive-date=December 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222191919/http://www.elnuevodia.com/zuleykaybareaterminaronsurelacion-1493649.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the summer of 2013, Barea started dating actress and [[Miss Universe Puerto Rico 2011]] [[Viviana Ortiz]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.metro.pr/entretener/viviana-y-barea-estan-superfelices/pGXnce!08WSXVQwA1p/|title=Viviana y Barea están "superfelices"|work=Metro.pr|date=March 5, 2014|access-date=March 5, 2014|language=es|archive-date=July 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712232803/http://www.metro.pr/entretener/viviana-y-barea-estan-superfelices/pGXnce!08WSXVQwA1p/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In February 2016, they confirmed that they were expecting their first child.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://primerahora.com/entretenimiento/farandula/nota/bareaconfirmaquetendraunaninaconvivianaortiz-1136278/|title=Barea confirma que tendrá una niña con Viviana Ortiz|work=primerahora.com |date=February 11, 2016|access-date=February 11, 2016|language=es}}</ref> Their daughter Paulina Barea Ortiz was born on March 31, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/bareayvivianaortizseconviertenenpadres-2181404/|title=Barea y Viviana Ortíz se convierten en padres|work=[[El Nuevo Día]]|date=April 1, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2016|language=es}}</ref> Barea and Ortiz got married on August 20, 2016, in a lavish ceremony at the church of the [[Universidad del Sagrado Corazón]] in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/entretenimiento/farandula/nota/atodolujolabodadevivianaortizyjjbarea-2226924/|title=El Nuevo Día|date=August 3, 2016|publisher=ElNuevoDia.com|language=es}}</ref>

Five days after [[Hurricane Maria]] hit, Barea spoke to his parents on a family friend's phone to inform them that Mavs owner [[Mark Cuban]] lent him the team plane to fly down to Puerto Rico the next day with food, water, and supplies. The Mavs' team plane made the trip five times, delivering a total of more than 100,000 pounds of food, water, power generators, and other supplies. Barea made the trip once while his stay-at-home wife ran the other four trips and focused full-time on the relief efforts. Barea's efforts in helping Puerto Rico earned him the NBA's J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award and the Hall of Fame's Mannie Jackson Award recognizing human spirit.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/mavs-jj-barea-wins-pbwa-citizenship-award/246016/|title=Mavs JJ Barea Wins PBWA Citizenship Award|date=June 13, 2018|access-date=June 20, 2025|work=[[NBCDFW]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526090856/https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/mavs-jj-barea-wins-pbwa-citizenship-award/246016/|archive-date=May 26, 2024|url-status=live|last=Nichelson|first=Charles}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2018/07/12/mavs-g-j-j-barea-named-one-of-the-winners-of-basketball-s-human-spirit-award-for-hurricane-relief-efforts-in-puerto-rico/|title=Mavs G J.J. Barea named one of the winners of basketball's human spirit award for hurricane relief efforts in Puerto Rico|date=July 11, 2018|access-date=June 20, 2025|work=[[Dallas Morning News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930093027/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2018/07/12/mavs-g-j-j-barea-named-one-of-the-winners-of-basketball-s-human-spirit-award-for-hurricane-relief-efforts-in-puerto-rico/|archive-date=September 30, 2022|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Barea is 12 credits short of getting his college degree from Northeastern. His older brothers are Jaime, a doctor, and Jason, an engineer. Barea returns to his hometown Mayagüez only a few times a year, and usually stops first in Barrio Paris, a poorer part of town where his father used to drive daily to pick up his teammates. Before the hurricane, his foundation focused on refurbishing basketball courts in poor areas. He holds several basketball clinics each summer throughout the island and usually donates uniforms and equipment for the youth leagues run by Tommy Zapata, who coached Barea from when he was a 3-year-old who could dribble the ball ambidextrously.<ref name="ESPN"/>
